children: The single Hetzner ARM64 box that runs Barkpark in production at api.barkpark.cloud.

instance — ARM64, idling at roughly 1GB RAM — reachable at 89.167.28.206 and served publicly as api.barkpark.cloud. The whole app lives under /opt/barkpark. It is a deliberately modest single-node footprint: one box hosts the Phoenix API, the Indx Engine, and Postgres together.

The running app is the systemd Service barkpark.service, which boots Phoenix API on :4000. In front of it sits Caddy, terminating TLS with a single ACME cert and proxying both :4000 and the Indx port :5001. Because Caddy owns HTTPS, Phoenix never sets force_ssl — that is the scar that once caused a 301 redirect loop.

Production co-hosts the Indx Engine, so the same box answers both content queries and retriever-seam requests. Background work — Webhooks dispatch, the Edge Projector, and the Indx indexer — runs on the Oban Worker runtime inside the same BEAM. Schema changes reach prod through Migration (mix ecto.migrate), and code changes through Deploy.
A correct deploy must satisfy the Fresh Install Invariant: with every plugin off, prod still serves the core Content Model. After any change, smoke-test the live HTTP API v1 before walking away.

Several surfaces orient themselves around this one origin. The Web Demo on barkpark.cloud pins its Vercel functions to region fra1 precisely to sit close to this Hetzner box and keep round-trips short. The Go TUI's pdrender is compiled by the prod post-merge build, which is why its go.mod is held at go 1.24.2 — a bump risks breaking the build here. And LiveView Studio runs inside this same box; its documented click-dead failure (a PHX_HOST/check_origin drift after a TLS cutover) is a Production failure mode.
